claim: Critical thinking was defined by expert consensus as skills plus dispositions, but the split was proposed before it was tested; the 1990 Delphi panel itself said correlations between them were unmeasured.
agent_test: None needed; design vocabulary only.

claim: Disposition scales and skill tests correlate only weakly to moderately in humans (r about .29 in adolescents; working memory r=.35 predicts CT as well or better; cross-lagged beta .28 WM vs .15 dispositions).
agent_test: Measure whether a prompted 'be open-minded' disposition changes accuracy beyond the plain model at equal tokens.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Self-report disposition measures are inflated by same-method bias and confidence; they are weak evidence of behaviour.
agent_test: Compare a model's self-rated disposition score with its behaviour on probes (belief change on evidence).

claim: LLMs score at or above human norms on disposition questionnaires (CTDS, AOT) yet fail applied tasks (belief bias, bias blind spot); stated and shown disposition come apart.
agent_test: Run AOT-style items and a behavioural twin on the agent; report the gap.

claim: Intrinsic self-correction (revise with no outside signal) does not help reasoning and often lowers accuracy (GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1; GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 89.0).
agent_test: Equal-token A/B: blind 'review your answer' vs signal-fired revise.

claim: Self-correction works when the trigger or feedback comes from outside the generator (oracle labels, tools, code, tests), not from the model's own judgement.
agent_test: Compare revise-on-code-failure vs revise-on-self-doubt at equal tokens.

claim: The bottleneck in self-correction is finding the error, not fixing it: given the error location, correction works; unaided, step-level mistake finding by GPT-4 reached only 52.87% overall (a20 figures 87.73 etc. are no-mistake-trace accuracy, corrected).
agent_test: Have code locate the failing step, model only repair; compare with model-located.

claim: Models show a self-correction blind spot: they fix an error in user text more than the same error in their own output (64.5% average over 14 non-reasoning models); a 'Wait' cue cut it 89.3%.
agent_test: Test whether a signal-gated 'Wait' beats an always-on one on injected and natural errors.

claim: Forced or unsignalled doubt costs accuracy; in our own word-puzzle test plain 92% vs forced doubt 75%.
agent_test: STILL OPEN: our 92% vs 75% has no recorded n or CI. Indirect support only: Jittham 2026 (reconsideration checkpoints lower accuracy) and CRITIC (no-tool self-critique small gains). No head-to-head of code-fired vs prompt-fired doubt exists.

claim: Sycophancy is the opposite failure of the willingness-to-revise disposition: models drop correct answers under challenge (Claude 1.3 admits mistakes on 98%; 'Are you sure?' lowers accuracy up to 27%). Replicated with reasoning-class models: pressure still flips them (Li 2026 nine models; Jittham 2026 mean accuracy -6.3 pp, o3 -7.0, R1 -6.0).
agent_test: Challenge-without-evidence probe: count flips from right to wrong with and without a requirement to cite output.

claim: Update rate alone is a poor open-mindedness score: of rebuttal-driven flips 43.5% moved to correct and 14.7% to wrong (SycEval); some one-sided arguments move models the wrong way (MillStone).
agent_test: Score updates split by evidence-driven vs pressure-driven change.

claim: Open-mindedness without a quality filter is gullibility: authoritative text easily sways LLM stance, and refusal dispositions vanish once any argument is supplied. Only opinion issues without ground truth were tested.
agent_test: Feed true and false 'authoritative' arguments; measure discrimination.

claim: Larger scale and RLHF can worsen the deference disposition (PaLM sycophancy up 19.8% from 8B to 62B; instruction tuning +26.0%); preference data reward agreement.
agent_test: Hide stance from judges; compare agreeing rate with and without stance visible.

claim: Judges favour their own output, so a self-critic lacks fair-mindedness toward its work (GPT-4 73.5% self-recognition; preference tracks recognition). Added: bias follows familiarity (low perplexity) as well as authorship (GPT-4 bias 0.749); GPT-4 recognises its own text 73.5% out of the box.
agent_test: Judge with authorship hidden vs visible at equal tokens.

claim: Chain-of-thought is not a faithful record of the disposition at work: biasing features cut accuracy up to 36% without being mentioned.
agent_test: Do not score disposition from stated reasoning; score from outcome under controlled biasing.

claim: Teaching raises critical-thinking scores modestly (Abrami 2015 g=0.30; 0.57 content-specific CT; only g=0.23 for dispositions), dialogue+application+mentoring best (g=0.57). Single quasi-experiments with d above 3 are test-matched and not transferable.
agent_test: Count only gains on unfitted held-out items.

claim: Doubt-type dispositions (reflective skepticism) are the hardest to train; openness moved, skepticism did not (small uncontrolled n=16 study).
agent_test: Prefer code-fired doubt to a trained urge to doubt.

claim: Sensitivity to the occasion (noticing when to think) is a distinct component from skill and inclination, and most thinking failures are sensitivity failures. Primary source not opened.
agent_test: Measure miss rate: items where a trigger was present and the agent did not fire.

claim: Metacognition correlates strongly with CT skill (r=.649, 60 effects from 24 articles), more than dispositions do; likely inflated by same-method self-report.
agent_test: Compare monitoring step vs no monitoring step at equal tokens.

claim: Actively open-minded thinking predicts accuracy beyond ability in humans (information seeking, forecasting). All sources are recalled or second-hand. New primary evidence (Haran 2013, N=183/220/200): the benefit runs through more information search; with fixed information AOT predicted nothing (all B<=0.112, p>=.10).
agent_test: Boundary condition read; stays single-source for the 'beyond ability' part (no ability control reported in Haran; Stanovich and West 1997 not opened, d17).

claim: LLM skill on argument critique is high when asked directly (o1-preview 81.25% on Ennis-Weir, one item, author-scored) but LLM grading of argument-quality subskills is unreliable (Krippendorff alpha .23 to .74; GPT-5 few-shot accuracy .532 vs fine-tuned Llama 8B .604).
agent_test: Compare model-judged argument quality with code-checked claims.

claim: Reflective habit emerges with scale and chain-of-thought: CRT correct humans 38%, davinci-003 5%, ChatGPT-3.5 59%, ChatGPT-4 96%.
agent_test: Check on the target model.

claim: Telling a model to be aware of bias helps little; restructuring the input (self-help rewrite) helps more (0-6% biased prompts remained).
agent_test: Compare 'be unbiased' instruction vs structural input rewrite.

claim: Model confidence is a weak doubt trigger: P(IK) generalises poorly to new tasks; in reasoning models confidence clusters at 93-95% and a confidence-gated defence gave no gain (GPT-5.1 98.50% baseline vs 98.39%); ChatGPT fails to defend correct answers even when 100% self-consistent.
agent_test: Compare confidence-fired doubt vs signal-fired doubt.

claim: Humans inherit LLM errors (24 participants; wrong medium-length explanations caught 54%, short 25%, long 31%), so fluent earlier text should not act as authority.
agent_test: Small workshop study; no direct agent test.

claim: GenAI-supported learning raises student CT scores on average (g=0.544) but the prediction interval [-0.588, 1.677] includes zero.
agent_test: Not relevant to agent design.

claim: Reasoning-class models still capitulate under challenge, though less than non-reasoning ones: 8 of 9 reasoning models beat GPT-4o on multi-turn consistency (d=0.12 to 0.40), and a suggested wrong answer is the strongest attack on all nine; Self-Doubt and Social Conformity cause 50% of failures.
agent_test: Run a challenge probe on the target model; count right-to-wrong flips with and without a suggested wrong answer.

claim: A 'Wait' cue still helps a reasoning-class model (s1-32B AIME24 50% to 57%), so unconditional re-check cues are not useless; but nobody has compared an unconditional cue with a signal-gated one at equal tokens.
agent_test: Equal-token head-to-head: always-Wait vs Wait only when a code signal fires.

claim: Behavioural disposition scores for LLMs exist only for resistance (Turn of Flip, Number of Flip, flip rate under 'Are you sure?', FlipFlop 46% flips and 17% accuracy drop), not for evidence-driven change; none is validated against a human disposition scale.
agent_test: Build a two-sided score: flips on correct answers (bad) vs fixes on wrong answers given real evidence (good).

claim: Argument form moves models more than source credibility: logical-sounding false appeals gave the highest misinformed rates (GPT-4 robustness 79.3 vs ChatGPT 49.9, Vicuna-7B 36.3). Whether models separate true from false authoritative arguments is untested.
agent_test: Pair true and false arguments of the same form and length; check whether the flip rate differs.

claim: Telling a judge to audit works much better in reasoning-class models: ProcessBench F1 o1-mini 87.9 vs GPT-4o 61.9 on natural first-error finding. The miss rate with no audit instruction is still unmeasured.
agent_test: Measure how often the trigger fires on natural errors when the model is not asked to audit.

claim: Hiding authorship alone is unlikely to remove self-preference: judges favour low-perplexity (familiar) text whether or not self-written, and GPT-4 recognises its own text 73.5% of the time.
agent_test: Test blind vs unblind judging plus a style-neutral rewrite at equal tokens.

claim: A checklist of critical-thinking questions (CQoT) gave about +5% on MT-Bench reasoning and math across five LLMs, with extra compute and a tiny benchmark; the best prompt-level analogue of teaching dispositions, but not an equal-token test.
agent_test: Replicate on a larger single-answer set with matched tokens.
